μασχαλ-ίζω ,
A.put under the arm-pits: hence, mutilate a corpse, since murderers believed that by cutting off the extremities (nose, ears, etc.), stringing them together, and passing the string round the neck and under the arm-pits of the victim they would avert vengeance, A. Ch. 439 (lyr., Pass. ), S. El. 445 ( Pass. ), cf. Ar.Byz. ap. Phot. , Suid.
s.v. μασχαλίσματα , EM 118.29 , * 574.202 , etc.
From A Greek-English Lexicon (Henry George Liddell, Robert Scott, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1940)
